hooks.prompt: A git commit is about to run. Review the STAGED changes before allowing it. Steps: (1) Run `git diff --cached` to see exactly what will be committed. If the diff is empty, verify with `git status` — if nothing is staged, approve (nothing to review). (2) Review the staged diff for CRITICAL and HIGH issues per the project's code-review standards: hardcoded secrets/credentials/API keys, SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, auth bypasses, data-loss risks, unhandled errors that could crash, and leftover debug/console statements. (3) DECISION: If you find any CRITICAL issue (security vulnerability or data-loss risk), BLOCK the commit and explain each finding with file:line and a concrete fix. If you find only HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW issues, APPROVE but list them as warnings so the developer can decide. Keep the review scoped strictly to the staged diff — do not review unrelated existing code. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

A git push is about to run. Review the commits that will be pushed before allowing it. Steps: (1) Determine what will be pushed: run `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}` to find the upstream; if it succeeds, diff with `git diff @{u}..HEAD`; if there is no upstream (new branch), diff against the default branch with `git diff origin/HEAD..HEAD` (fall back to `git diff origin/main..HEAD` or `git diff origin/master..HEAD`). If the diff is empty, approve (nothing new to review). (2) Review the outgoing diff for CRITICAL and HIGH issues per the project's code-review standards: hardcoded secrets/credentials/API keys, SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, auth bypasses, data-loss risks, unhandled errors, and leftover debug statements. Prefer the review-pr skill's rigor if available. (3) DECISION: If you find any CRITICAL issue, BLOCK the push and explain each finding with file:line and a concrete fix. If you find only HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW issues, APPROVE but list them as warnings. Scope the review to the outgoing commits only. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS
